title: Packaging & Metadata Deployment
source: ../Salesforce App builder/Salesforce App Builder Roadmap/developer Platform App Builder Roadmap/15-Packaging-Metadata-Deployment.md
html: ��# 15. Packaging & Metadata Deployment ## Learning objectives - Explain metadata and how Salesforce stores configuration - Distinguish package types (managed 2GP, unlocked, org packages/unmanaged) at App Builder level - Describe the manifest (package.xml) and what it contains - Differentiate source format vs metadata format and when to deploy source - Compare sf project deploy vs legacy sfdx commands (conceptually) and know when destructive changes are needed - Identify common deployment issues and how to validate before deployment ## 1. What is metadata? Metadata is your org configuration (objects, fields, layouts, flows, record types, profiles, permission sets, etc.)  the setup, not the data records. ## 2. Package types (key distinctions) | Package type | Purpose | Upgradeable | Locked | Typical use | |---|---|---|---|---| | Unmanaged | Share/distribute source | No | No | Open source/templates, one-off moves | | Managed (2GP) | ISV/AppExchange | Yes | IP-protected | Commercial apps | | Unlocked | Internal modular distribution | Yes (upgrades) | No | Internal reusable packages, modular org architecture | For Platform App Builder, focus on when to use unlocked/unmanaged for internal work and understanding managed vs unlocked. ## 3. package.xml (manifest) The package.xml defines what metadata is retrieved/deployed. Key elements: types (name, members), version. Example minimal: xml <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <Package xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <types> <members>Brightline_Sales_User</members> <name>PermissionSet</name> </types> <version>58.0</version> </Package> ## 4. Source format vs metadata format - Source format: decomposed, versionable in Git (force-app/main/default/*)  used in modern SFDX projects. - Metadata format: zipped package (retrieve/deploy via Ant/legacy packaging). ## 5. Deployment approaches - sf project deploy start: deploy source format to org (scratch/sandbox/prod in appropriate contexts). Local only in this project. - Validation first when possible; destructive changes require separate manifest. - Order matters in some cases (dependencies). ## 6. Common gotchas - Missing dependencies (referenced fields/objects) - Profiles/permission sets need careful handling - Flow versions and active flows - Validation rules blocking test data - Test coverage not required for most declarative-only deployments, but can affect in managed contexts. ## Exercises 15.1 Identify when to use unlocked vs unmanaged package. 15.2 Interpret a simple package.xml. 15.3 Determine if a change needs destructive changes.
